title: Governed Inference QBR: Metrics & Evaluation Framework
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes a repeatable, governed framework for quarter‑by‑quarter customer QBRs focused on inference health, LLM evaluation, and operational signals. The goal is to give Customer Success (CS), Engineering, and Product a shared set of metrics, evaluation artifacts, dashboards, and playbooks so QBR conversations are evidence‑driven and actionable.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and Customer Reliability Engineers (CREs)
- Product owners responsible for model and feature roadmaps
- Engineering owners for serving runtime and telemetry pipelines

Scope
- Hosted and Dedicated customers; guidance includes private deployment considerations where telemetry may be delayed or sampled.
- Metrics span cost, latency, availability, quality (evaluations), and request patterns that drive economics.

Key Outcomes for a QBR using this framework
1) Shared indicator set with one golden dashboard per customer.
2) Actionable health classifications (Green/Amber/Red) with recommended runbook steps.
3) A reproducible evaluation snapshot (prompt set, baseline model, scoring summary).

Governed Metric Set (minimum required)
| Metric | Purpose | Owner | Frequency | Threshold (Amber) | Threshold (Red) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P50 P95 token latency (inference) | Customer perceived responsiveness | infra-serving | daily | P95 > 350ms | P95 > 700ms | Break out by route/model variant |
| Request success rate (2xx/total) | Availability signal | sre | 10m | < 99.5% | < 98.0% | Include 5xx and 429 rates separately |
| Tokens per USD (cost efficiency) | Cost economics | finance/cs | weekly | 10% degradation vs baseline | 25% degradation | Compute per-route and model family |
| Eval pass rate (gold prompt suite) | Quality regression detector | cs/product | per-release | delta < 2% | delta > 5% | See Eval snapshot section below |
| Embedding similarity drift | Semantic regressions in retrieval | product | daily | cosine drop > 0.02 | cosine drop > 0.05 | Compare to rolling 30d baseline |
| Prefix cache hit rate | Cost/latency optimization | infra | hourly | < 60% | < 40% | Indicative of prompt variability |

Data sources and instrumentation
- Golden dashboards must be composed from: API access logs, model runtime metrics (GPU tail latencies, queue lengths), cost attribution (token-level billing), and evaluation harness outputs.
- For Private deployments: collect the same artifacts via the customer telemetry agent; if sampling is required, include sampling multiplier metadata in the dashboard.

Evaluation snapshot (what to store for each QBR)
- Baseline model name and exact version (e.g., redwood/gptx-rlhf@2026-01-20)
- Prompt set: canonical list of N=150 prompts representing high-impact flows (attach as CSV).
- Scoring rubric: automated metrics (exact match/F1, BLEU for structured data, embedding cosine for semantic retrieval) and human annotations for top 10 failure cases.
- Eval summary: pass rate, false negative rate, top 5 failure prompts with short transcripts.

Example evaluation artifact (CSV header)
prompt_id,prompt_text,expected_label,model_version,automated_score,human_flag,notes

Dashboard templates and sections (minimum panes)
1) Executive summary: SLO status, cost delta, top 3 risks.
2) Latency & availability: heatmaps by region/model, P50/P95/P99.
3) Cost breakdown: tokens, embeddings, per-route unit economics.
4) Quality & evals: pass rate trend, per-prompt failure list.
5) Usage patterns: spikes, client SDK versions, burst sources.
6) Action items & owners.

Suggested SQL/BigQuery examples
- 7‑day P95 token latency per model\
```
SELECT model_name, APPROX_QUANTILES(token_latency_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_latency_ms
FROM `redwood_prod.api_logs`
WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY model_name;
```

- Eval pass rate per release tag\
```
SELECT release_tag, COUNTIF(pass) / COUNT(1) AS pass_rate
FROM `redwood_prod.evals.results`
WHERE eval_suite = 'qbr-golden-150' AND event_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY release_tag
ORDER BY event_date DESC;
```

Health classification and recommended QBR actions
- Green: All core SLOs met. Action: continue trend monitoring; highlight positive optimizations.
- Amber: One or more SLOs breached at Amber. Action: open a short remediation ticket and schedule a 72‑hour stabilization plan (see Remediation Runbook).
- Red: Critical SLO or quality regression. Action: immediate incident coordination with CS, SRE, and Product; consider temporary model rollback or rate limiting.

Remediation Runbook (72‑hour stabilization)
1) Triage (within 1 hour): Confirm metric source; capture log window and sampling. Owner: CRE.
2) Containment (within 4 hours): If quality regression, pin production traffic to previous model version or enable fallback routing. If latency/capacity, enable burst capacity or autoscale policy. Owner: infra-serving oncall.
3) Mitigation (24 hours): Apply prompt-level mitigations (truncate inputs, enforce early-cache keys), adjust batching policy, or temporarily increase compute commit. Owner: engineering and CS.
4) Recovery verification (48–72 hours): Re-run golden evals, monitor pass rate and latency trend, and validate cost impact. Owner: CS + infra.
5) Post‑mortem and QBR action item creation.

Ownership and cadence
- CSM (primary): prepares customer narrative, highlights business impact, and tracks action items.
- CRE (telemetry & triage): provides data pulls, golden dashboard, and supports oncall during the quarter.
- Product (quality owner): curates the prompt suite and reviews eval rubric.
- SRE/Infra: provides availability/latency context and executes runtime mitigations.

QBR Preparation checklist (2 weeks before meeting)
1) Verify data completeness for the quarter (CSM + CRE). 2) Run the golden eval suite and attach results to QBR deck. 3) Confirm proposed action items and owners. 4) Smoke test the dashboard links and include reproducible queries. 5) Share pre-read with customer 3 business days before QBR.

Example action triggers (automated)
- Auto-create ticket when eval pass rate drops by >3% vs rolling 14d baseline.
- Create cost alert when tokens per USD drop by >15% month-over-month on a customer route.
- Auto-assign CRE when prefix cache hit rate < 40% for >6 hours.

Appendix: Template subject lines and pre-reads
- Email subject: "[QBR] Inference Health & Action Items — Q1 2026 — <Customer Name>"
- Pre-read attachment list: golden_eval_summary.csv, dashboard_links.md, cost_snapshot.pdf, proposed_actions.xlsx
